title: NOX4 promotes cardiomyocyte ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy in associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired NRF2 nuclear translocation.
authors: Qin, Sirun; Chen, Chenyang; Wang, Xinran; Deng, Lijie; Wang, Jian; Zhu, Can; Zhu, Chaoying; Cao, Yu; Zhang, Song
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NOX4在脓毒症心肌病中促进铁死亡相关损伤的机制，核心为细胞氧化应激与线粒体功能，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Septic cardiomyopathy is a common early complication of sepsis, and its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic differential expression analysis, a ferroptosis gene set, protein-protein interaction networks, and consensus machine-learning-based screening to identify NOX4 as a core ferroptosis-related candidate gene. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed that NOX4 upregulation was most pronounced in cardiomyocytes and was accompanied by enhanced intercellular communication. In the cecal ligation and puncture mouse model, pharmacological inhibition of NOX4 with Setanaxib improved survival and cardiac function, reduced myocardial injury biomarkers, alleviated histopathological damage, and partially reversed the dysregulation of ferroptosis-related markers. In the lipopolysaccharide-stimulated cardiomyocyte model, Setanaxib treatment or genetic silencing with si-NOX4 mitigated the accumulation of ferrous iron, lipid peroxidation, and reactive oxygen species, and partially restored the expression of NRF2, GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4. Mechanistically, NOX4 inhibition attenuated mitochondrial dysfunction, including mitochondrial membrane depolarization, fragmentation, and respiratory dysfunction, and restored nuclear NRF2 levels and downstream antioxidant signaling. In addition, candidate compounds identified from the HERB database and evaluated by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were predicted to exhibit stable binding features with NOX4. Collectively, these findings support a model in which NOX4 contributes to ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy in association with mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired NRF2-dependent antioxidant signaling.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症心肌病是脓毒症常见的早期并发症，其潜在机制尚未完全阐明。在本研究中，我们整合了转录组差异表达分析、铁死亡基因集、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络以及基于共识机器学习筛选，将NOX4鉴定为核心铁死亡相关候选基因。单细胞转录组分析进一步揭示，NOX4上调在心肌细胞中最为显著，并伴随细胞间通讯增强。在盲肠结扎穿刺小鼠模型中，使用Setanaxib对NOX4进行药理学抑制可改善生存率和心脏功能，降低心肌损伤生物标志物，减轻组织病理学损伤，并部分逆转铁死亡相关标志物的失调。在脂多糖刺激的心肌细胞模型中，Setanaxib处理或si-NOX4基因沉默可缓解亚铁离子积累、脂质过氧化和活性氧产生，并部分恢复NRF2、GPX4、SLC7A11和ACSL4的表达。机制上，NOX4抑制减轻了线粒体功能障碍，包括线粒体膜去极化、碎片化和呼吸功能障碍，并恢复核内NRF2水平及下游抗氧化信号。此外，从HERB数据库中鉴定并通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟评估的候选化合物，被预测与NOX4表现出稳定的结合特征。综合来看，这些发现支持一个模型，即NOX4通过线粒体功能障碍和NRF2依赖性抗氧化信号受损，促进脓毒症心肌病中的铁死亡相关损伤。
